items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Freddie Greene was there on guitar, and

ctx.x: I've got to get to one of the most exciting record dates, and a definite high point in my career. I was called by -- I don't remember whom, to do a record date while I was on the Hit Parade, and I had a record in front of me, and if you wait until I research, I'll give you the year.

Well, there is no date on the album, but I think it was around '55. I was called for a record date at Carnegie Hall rehearsal hall, that's where it took place and they had set up equipment there, and when I walked in, I was flabbergasted the people on the date. In the first place, I walked in - and I always walk in early to set up the drums; there was Walter Pope there, and we said greetings and Joe Newman was there, and we had just begun to know each other, really; and Lawrence Brown on trombone; Pete Brown on…
I was the only white on the date, and this was -- well, the date was Joe Turner's, and the name of the album, which is a collector's item, is The Boss of the Blues.
